transcript.text:
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's workout meeting on the Harbor Point Properties restructuring proposal. As you know, we have an $8 million term loan secured by the borrower's office building, equipment, and receivables. Harbor Point has requested a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral due to weaker-than-expected occupancy reducing their debt-service coverage.

Before I can record any final terms, I need each of you to walk through your review findings. Let's go through the standard agenda: risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management. For each area, please provide your findings update and identify the supporting document or policy behind any recommendation you make. I'll make sure the relevant sources are captured in the meeting minutes.

Let's start with the risk review. What are you seeing on the current covenant test and the applicable workout treatment?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from the covenant testing file I reviewed this week. Harbor Point's leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level. Under our workout policy, a covenant waiver is only allowed with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months the borrower requested — and requires a monthly leverage certificate as an ongoing condition. I should also note that I have not yet attached the testing file to the committee package, so I want to make sure everyone is aware of these findings now. The bottom line is that the borrower's 12-month extension request exceeds what the workout policy permits for a waiver, and the monthly leverage certificate would need to be part of any restructured terms.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important update from the relationship side. This morning I received a signed term sheet from Harbor Point committing the owners to inject exactly $1,200,000 of new equity at restructuring closing. This commitment has not yet been entered in the relationship system, so I want to make sure it's on the record now. This equity injection could be relevant to Elena's final decision on the restructuring terms, particularly given Jonas's findings on the covenant breach and the workout policy constraints.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical legal finding to share. While reviewing the intercreditor agreement this week, I confirmed that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested. This directly impacts the borrower's request to release $900,000 of equipment collateral — we cannot proceed with that release until the senior lender provides written consent, and we haven't even initiated that request yet. The supporting document here is the intercreditor agreement.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I completed a collateral review yesterday, and my findings are significant for this restructuring. The review showed that receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package. Under our collateral policy, this requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout the extension period. I should also note that I have not yet updated the monitoring schedule to reflect this requirement. Given Jonas's point that the workout policy limits the extension to 9 months rather than the requested 12, and the collateral policy's weekly borrowing-base certificate requirement, these are important conditions that need to be incorporated into any final terms Elena records. The supporting document here is the collateral policy.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Initiate written consent request to senior lender for equipment collateral release before any future release can be considered.
Update the monitoring schedule to reflect the weekly borrowing-base certificate requirement throughout the extension period.
Attach the covenant testing file to the committee package.
Enter the signed $1,200,000 equity injection term sheet into the relationship system.
